quote: When I woke up to-day and got up and dressed myself, I suddenly began to feel as if everything in this life was open to me, and that I knew how I must live.
source: Anton Chekhov, The Three Sisters, Act I (Irina) (trans. Julius West, 1916)
speaker: Irina

evidence.where: Full text of the West translation downloaded and searched; the sentence was read in place at the head of Irina's speech to Chebutikin, inside the Act I block, and the title page and translator credit were read in the same file.
evidence.edition: Plays by Anton Tchekoff, Second Series, trans. Julius West (Charles Scribner's Sons, and Duckworth, 1916)
evidence.locator: Act I, Irina to Ivan Romanovitch Chebutikin on her name-day, the sentence opening the speech that goes on to 'A man must work, toil in the sweat of his brow'

reason: Located word for word, hyphenated 'to-day' and all, in Act I of West's text, with the speech prefix IRINA and Chebutikin's reply on either side. Chekhov stands at two of three in the year, so a third line is within the cap, and the speech is Irina's waking and not her later disappointment.
